proposals.title: ADR-009 document and CanonicalEncoder implementation in core
proposals.why_now: FASE-1 acceptance criteria explicitly state 'ADR-009 escrito e o encoder implementado antes de qualquer hash de estado existir'. StateHash and SaveHash cannot be defined, tested, or validated until the canonical encoding specification exists and is implemented. This blocks INV-22 and all replay invariants. No ADRs have been written yet; two DEFINIR items (hash function from ADR-002, and the CanonicalEncoder spec from ADR-009 itself) must be resolved before any hash-producing code is authored. Doing this first prevents the most dangerous form of retroactive damage: changing the encoder after state hashes already exist.

proposals.why_now: All domain computation in world, domain, and application depends on Money, Quantity, Price, Rate (bigint-branded), Tick (safe-number-branded), and the positional RNG. Without these, neither the price generator nor the ledger can be written in a type-safe, determinism-enforcing way. This is the second dependency after IDEA-001, since the RNG uses the hash function resolved in that ADR.

proposals.title: Market price generator for two assets in packages/world
proposals.why_now: The tick loop in application cannot be constructed until world can produce worldPrice(assetId, tick). The price generator — trendLayer, idiosyncraticNoise with octave-based block interpolation, regimeAmplitude, and logPrice composition — is the defining component of the world package and enables INV-02 and INV-03, both required for FASE-1. Two assets (ORB and NEXA) satisfy the FASE-1 minimum; all seven are FASE-2 scope. An ADR for octave count and generator parameters (DEFINIR from section 5.1) must be written alongside the implementation to prevent undocumented magic numbers from entering a versionable configuration file.

proposals.title: Multi-commodity double-entry ledger and market order execution in packages/domain
proposals.why_now: The tick loop requires domain to evaluate liquidations, execute orders, and compute equity. The ledger is the accounting backbone of every economic operation. INV-04 through INV-07 are FASE-1 acceptance criteria and can only be tested once the ledger and market order path exist. The rounding residue account (world:rounding_residue:<COMMODITY>) is particularly critical: money that disappears in rounding is a bug by spec, and the mechanism that prevents it must be built into the first transaction that ever commits.

proposals.title: Canonical tick loop and save format in packages/application plus tools/replay
proposals.why_now: The 10-step tick processing order is TRAVADO and must be implemented at a single, readable point in the code. Without it, INV-01 (replay == live session), INV-11 (1-tick == 100-tick == direct-jump), and INV-21 (save envelope integrity) cannot be tested — all required for FASE-1 acceptance. The replay CLI (tools/replay) is also a FASE-1 deliverable: it must be able to compare two executions and report the first divergent tick. tools/bench needs a frozen baseline ratio. Deferring the tick loop risks discovering ordering bugs only after the ledger and world generator have accumulated significant dependents.

repository_assessment.current_state: Infrastructure is complete: monorepo, TypeScript strict config, ESLint determinism lint rules, boundary dependency checker, CI pipeline, and test harness for tooling are all in place. All twelve product packages (packages/*, apps/desktop/*, tools/replay, tools/bench) contain only empty stubs (export {};). No ADRs have been written. No product implementation code exists.
repository_assessment.highest_priority_gap: The core package has no implementation whatsoever — no branded numeric types, no positional RNG, no CanonicalEncoder — and FASE-1 acceptance explicitly requires ADR-009 written and the encoder implemented before any state hash exists. Every other FASE-1 deliverable (world price generator, domain ledger, tick loop, replay CLI, INV-01 through INV-07, INV-22, INV-23) depends on core.
